09:00.headline: Measure it before you chase it
09:00.topic: Offseason development: baseline, pick 1-2 numbers, re-test, share real gains with coaches
09:00.caption:
Does your player know his numbers right now, or just roughly?

The offseason is the best time to get better. It's also the easiest time to lose track of whether the work is paying off.

⚾ Test his baseline: 60 time, exit velo, velo or pop time, whatever fits his position
⚾ Pick one or two numbers to improve, not ten
⚾ Re-test every 6 to 8 weeks under the same conditions
⚾ When a number really moves, update his profile and let coaches know

Measured progress is easier for a college coach to see than "he's been working hard."

Which number is he working on this winter?

13:00.headline: Grades are a recruiting tool
13:00.topic: Unpopular opinion: academics widen college options and support recruiting
13:00.caption:
Unpopular opinion: his report card is part of his recruiting profile.

Velo, exit velo and the 60 get the attention. But grades quietly shape how many college options your player has.

✅ Strong grades can widen his list of schools that fit
✅ Academic aid can matter, especially at levels where athletic money is limited
✅ Coaches notice players who won't be a risk to stay eligible

A few extra MPH can help. A strong GPA can open doors his numbers alone can't.

Agree or disagree? Tell us in the comments.
